_what: Deal-market activity inputs for the EWM's DMHI. Two legs with very different lags, kept separate on purpose.

hsr_tier_150_300m._source: FTC/DOJ HSR annual reports, Exhibit A Table I, brackets $150-200M + $200-300M, summed. US Government work.
hsr_tier_150_300m._why_this_band: The sale being timed is ~$200-225M. The spec's tier is $100-250M but the published bracket edges do not split at $250M, so $150-300M is the closest clean span.
hsr_tier_150_300m._why_no_threshold_correction: The HSR reporting threshold has never exceeded $133.9M (Feb 2026), which is BELOW this tier's $150M floor. Every deal in this band was reportable in every year, so the threshold erosion that contaminates the TOTAL count does not touch it. No correction is applied and none is needed.
hsr_tier_150_300m._lag: ~10 months. FY2025 (ending Sep-2025) published Jul-2026. This is an ANCHOR, never a live signal - the GF Data pattern.
hsr_tier_150_300m._basis: Totals to ADJUSTED transactions (those in which a second request could have been issued), not transactions reported.

edgar_merger_proxies._source: SEC EDGAR quarterly form index; DEFM14A + PREM14A, counted as DISTINCT ACCESSION NUMBERS (form.idx emits one row per filer; counting rows inflates some forms up to 8.7x).
edgar_merger_proxies._lag: ~1 day. This is the LIVE leg.
edgar_merger_proxies._proxy_gap: These are PUBLIC-TARGET deals going to a shareholder vote, of all sizes. The sale being timed is a private mid-market company. This leg stands in for private-market conditions and is not a measurement of them - label it as such wherever it is shown.
edgar_merger_proxies._baseline_starts: 1997Q1 - EDGAR filing became mandatory in May 1996, so earlier counts measure adoption, not deal-making.
